result.summary:
STEP 0.5 REGISTRY LOOKUP: no prior resolved issue matches this symptom. Searched docs/issues/*.yaml for OIDC/role-revocation/live-enforcement-gap symptoms (grep for evaluate_access|map_verified_claims|RoleRegistry|authenticate_oidc|verify_api_token, plus a broader revoc/oidc/claim/deactivat sweep). Only 2 files reference any of the target symbols besides ISS-0736 itself: ISS-0116 and ISS-0112, both members of the unrelated tenant-schema-provisioning-flakiness family (ISS-0109 lineage) -- their symbol hits are incidental role_registry_test.exs mentions in a different investigation about sandbox/fixture migration, not about OIDC live-enforcement. No match found. Not a recurrence. Severity stays as filed (BLOCKER).

STEP 1 -- INDEPENDENT ROOT-CAUSE DIAGNOSIS (all read directly from source on this branch, not copied from ISS-0736.yaml's prose):

1. lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex `authenticate_oidc/2` (private, :125-136): a `with` chain -- verify_token -> extract_realm -> resolve_tenant -> guard_realm_ownership -> map_claims -> provision_user -- ending in `attach_auth_context(conn, tenant.id, provisioned.user.id, identity_context.roles)` (:132). CONFIRMED: the roles value attached to conn.assigns[:auth_context][:roles] is `identity_context.roles`, produced by step 4a's `map_claims/2` (:294-302) alone -- `provisioned` (the JIT-provisioned/looked-up DB `User` struct from step 4b, `provision_user/3` at :311-326) is used ONLY for its `.user.id`, never for any role or status field. There is no DB read of roles anywhere in this function.

2. lib/letflow/oidc/claim_mapping.ex `map_verified_claims/3` (:87-104): builds `%IdentityContext{... roles: resolve_roles(claims, config.roles_claim_paths), ...}` -- `resolve_roles/2` walks only the JWT `claims` map passed in by the caller (the bearer token's own decoded body) via `config.roles_claim_paths`; no Repo call, no argument that could reach a Letflow-local table. CONFIRMED: roles are derived exclusively from the token's own claims, freshly per request, with zero cross-check against any Letflow-local state.

3. lib/letflow/api/authorization.ex `evaluate_access/2` (:778-806): takes `%AccessContext{}` (built from conn.assigns[:auth_context], per caller convention) and branches purely on `ctx.roles`/`ctx.user_id` via `has_role?/2`/`has_permission?/2`/`is_task_worker_only?/1`. It has no DB dependency of its own -- it is a pure function over whatever role list it is handed. CONFIRMED: this is the sole authorization decision point and it trusts its caller's role list completely, so the defect is entirely upstream of this function, in what populates ctx.roles (step 1/2 above).

4. lib/letflow/identity/role_registry.ex moduledoc (:2-18): states verbatim 'This module has no coupling to the OIDC/claim-mapping pipeline: it does not alias or call any Letflow.Oidc.* module, and it does not call or get called by Letflow.Identity's OIDC-pipeline functions'. CONFIRMED verbatim as quoted in ISS-0736. This is the module backing web/src/pages/admin/UsersPage.tsx / GroupsPage.tsx's role/group assignment UI (per ISS-0736's affected_files; not independently re-verified against the .tsx files this run, out of scope for Step 1's source list) -- so whatever a tenant_admin does through that GUI's role assignment writes to `tenant_role`/`groups` tables this module owns, and nothing downstream ever reads them for an OIDC session.

5. lib/letflow/identity.ex `provision_oidc_user/4` (:125-136) and its private callees `upsert_by_external_identity/4` (:1467-1475) -> `insert_or_fetch/4` (:1477 onward): CONFIRMED `attach_auth_context`'s roles argument traces back to `identity_context.roles` (JWT-derived, per #2), never to the provisioned/looked-up `User` row. Further finding beyond ISS-0736's own text: `Letflow.Identity.User`'s schema (lib/letflow/identity/user.ex :36-47) has NO role field at all -- `username`, `display_name`, `email`, `password_hash`, `status` (Ecto.Enum :active/:inactive, default :active -- this is REQ-073's deactivation flag), `auth_source`, `external_id`, `external_realm`. There is nowhere on the `users` row itself to even store an OIDC user's role; roles live exclusively in `tenant_role`/`groups` (RoleRegistry's tables) with no join back to `users` exercised by the auth pipeline. ADDITIONALLY, and this widens the fix's required scope beyond ISS-0736's role-only framing: the `status` field (:active/:inactive) is also never read anywhere in auth_pipeline.ex (verified via grep -- the only 'status' hits in that file are HTTP status codes) or in provision_user/3's path. So a tenant_admin deactivating a user via POST /users/:id/status (REQ-073) ALSO has zero live effect on that user's already-issued OIDC session, via the exact same defect shape as the role-revocation gap ISS-0736 names. Both role changes and account deactivation need to be covered by whatever live check the fix adds -- not role alone.

6. PRECEDENT -- lib/letflow/identity.ex `verify_api_token/2` (:1152-1178, called from lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex `authenticate_api_token/2` :140-149 via `verify_token_credential/2` :219-224): signature `verify_api_token(plaintext :: String.t(), opts :: opts()) :: {:ok, %{user_id: Ecto.UUID.t(), roles: [String.t()]}} | {:error, :invalid} | {:error, :revoked} | {:error, :expired}`. Mechanism: hashes the plaintext token, does exactly one `Repo.get_by(ApiToken, [token_hash: token_hash], prefix: prefix)` per call -- no ETS, no process-dictionary cache, no periodic-refresh worker anywhere in the call path (moduledoc for this function states this explicitly, confirmed by reading the function body, :1157-1178). Branches on the freshly-read row: nil -> :invalid; non-nil revoked_at -> :revoked; expired expires_at -> :expired; else touches last_used_at best-effort and returns {:ok, %{user_id: token.user_id, roles: token.roles}} (:1180-1196) -- note `token.roles` here IS read live from the `api_tokens` row on every single call, which is exactly the shape the OIDC branch lacks for its own JWT-claims-only roles. This is the mechanism REQ-378/ISS-0736's fix_direction points at mirroring: one uncached `Repo` round trip per request, positioned so nothing can observe a pre-revocation value because there is no cache layer between the revoking UPDATE and the next request's read.

CORRECTIONS TO ISS-0736's OWN TEXT: none found -- every claim in ISS-0736's description (function names, line-level behavior, the RoleRegistry moduledoc quote, the zero-live-enforcement conclusion) checked out against independent reads on this branch. The one addition beyond its text is #5's `User.status` finding: the gap is not role-only, it also covers REQ-073 account deactivation, which shares the identical mechanism absence. CODE-DESIGNER's fix should give authenticate_oidc/2 a new step, positioned after step 4b's provision_user/3 (so it has both `provisioned.user.id` and `tenant_id`/`schema_name` available) and before attach_auth_context/4, that does a live, uncached, per-request Repo read of the OIDC-provisioned user's current status (users.status) and current effective roles (tenant_role/groups, RoleRegistry's tables, joined by user identity) -- mirroring verify_api_token/2's shape: one Repo round trip, no cache, short-circuit to a Deny401/403-mapped error tuple (via the same handle_auth_error/2 tagged-error convention every other step already uses) when status is :inactive or the resolved role set differs from what would otherwise be used. Exact join/lookup mechanism between users and tenant_role/groups is CODE-DESIGNER's design decision, not pre-decided here.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for a fix design covering REQ-378's acceptance criteria: add a live, uncached, per-request local-state check to authenticate_oidc/2 (lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex) mirroring Identity.verify_api_token/2's mechanism, covering both role/group changes (RoleRegistry-backed) and account status (users.status, REQ-073) -- see result.summary for exact function/line citations and the widened status-field scope finding.
